entries.sourceNarrationText: Compliance work often lives across spreadsheets, inboxes, and disconnected folders. That makes it difficult to see who owns the work, what evidence exists, and which gaps need attention. FeDril brings those readiness activities into one organized, No-CUI workspace.

Sound confident but not theatrical, exaggerated, or overly promotional. Use brief natural pauses between ideas. Clearly pronounce technical compliance terminology and acronyms. Maintain consistent volume, tone, pace, and delivery across all scenes.

entries.sourceNarrationText: Northstar Precision Systems is a fictional company used only for this demonstration. Its dashboard brings together the current readiness signal, overdue work, high-priority obligations, and evidence status. Teams can start with the items that need attention instead of reconciling several trackers before every review.

entries.sourceNarrationText: The obligation queue highlights a high-priority item tied to FAR 52.204-21. Opening the detail view keeps the plain-language action, source reference, expected evidence, current status, and related work together. FeDril supports the review process; it does not replace qualified compliance or legal judgment.

entries.sourceNarrationText: FeDril's current product posture is compliance management only. The evidence workspace presents a No-CUI notice and identifies prohibited sensitive content before the upload area. This demonstration does not upload a file. Teams should use synthetic, redacted, or non-sensitive information and follow their own approved handling procedures.

entries.sourceNarrationText: Server-authoritative permissions determine which actions each tenant member can perform. Compliance-relevant changes also create tenant-scoped audit events. The audit view gives reviewers a chronological record of activity without exposing another tenant's information. These controls support accountability; they do not certify an organization's compliance.
